time.method: 2010 minus 12,100 to 10,500 years; IRSL, not calibrated radiocarbon BP

claims.text: At Quarry of the Ancestors (HhOv-319), artifacts in a periglacial sediment sequence support early human activity near the Pleistocene–Holocene transition. Associated upper aeolian sand yielded an IRSL age of 11.3 ± 0.8 ka.
claims.explanation: Sediment age and archaeological stratigraphy constrain activity indirectly. This is neither an exact human-arrival date nor the date of Lake Agassiz flooding; Table 1 uses 2010 CE as datum.

support.note: Supports this scoped finding; no population size or named descendant identity inferred.

unresolved.reason: Publisher citation verified but full primary content unavailable in this review. Synopsis suppresses very large uncertainty: external governmental table lists 8475 ±650 RCYBP among multiple problematic dates. Do not plot 8475 as a secure exact calendar occupation age; obtain original dating discussion.
Reservoir Lakes, Cloquet Lake, Misiano/McDougal Lake, Big Rice Lake and Eveleth retained as leads only until primary site descriptions and dating are checked.

Anderson and Gillam 2000; Darvill 2018; Beaudoin 1996; Horta 2019 and other register entries without added claims require targeted primary review before additional site facts. Horta concerns Argentina and cannot establish North American shoreline occupation.

corrections.correction: No uniform 26–13.8 ka blockage or compulsory coastal itinerary is established here. Different sectors, physical access, ecology, and archaeological use require separate claims.

Woywitka 11.3 ±0.8 ka uses 2010 CE IRSL datum; the synopsis incorrectly labels it cal BP and conflates post-flood sediment with arrival and flood dates. Lesnek 2018 is not an Athabasca flood excavation source.
10,000–5,000 14C BP components do not establish continuous occupation; retained raw, not subtracted from 1950.
Coastal accessibility and model compatibility are not proof that all initial populations used a single coastal route.
Genetic bison movements are not evidence proving a human migration in the same direction.

review.deduplication: Compared live evidence/proposals plus six specified round3 sidecars by record IDs and source DOI. Existing Great Lakes, coastal models and northeastern records retained.
review.validation: All new records and independently applied updates pass validateRecord.
